topic.title: Nobody's Buying The iPhone In Cash Anymore
topic.claim: The iPhone 17 becoming India's best-selling phone isn't really an iPhone story, it's a credit story, people financing a month's salary through EMI while credit card spending hits ₹23.6 lakh crore like that's just how you buy things now.
topic.behaviour: iPhone 17 topped India's smartphone volume charts with over 4% market share, and during Big Billion Days prices dropped to ₹77,999-79,999 against the ₹99,900 MRP, driven heavily by no-cost EMI offers, while credit card spending hit a record ₹23.62 lakh crore in FY26, up nearly 12%, with monthly spends crossing ₹2 trillion for three straight months.
topic.mechanism: When EMI and credit cards make the sticker price invisible, people stop comparing the real cost of a purchase and start comparing the monthly number instead, and the monthly number always looks smaller than it is.
topic.group: Young professionals financing lifestyle and gadget purchases on EMI and credit cards
real_details: iPhone 17 topped India's smartphone volume charts in 2026 with over 4% market share
iPhone 17 prices dropped to ₹77,999-79,999 against the ₹99,900 MRP during Big Billion Days starting October 9
Indians spent ₹23.62 lakh crore on credit cards in FY2025-26, up nearly 12% from ₹21.09 lakh crore
monthly credit card spends crossed ₹2 trillion for three straight months
topic.news_peg: iPhone 17's Big Billion Days pricing (Oct 9, 2026) alongside the FY26 credit card spending record
topic.why_now: Both data points are current and festive EMI financing is peaking this month

paragraphs: The iPhone 17 is India's best-selling phone right now. Over 4% of every phone sold.
That's not an Apple story. That's a credit story. Nobody paid ₹99,900. They paid ₹8,667 a month and told themselves that's different.
During Big Billion Days the iPhone 17 dropped from ₹99,900 to around ₹77,999 if you had the right bank card.
But the number that actually moved it wasn't the discount. It was the no-cost EMI. Six months, nine months, split it up, start at ₹8,667.
A phone that costs most people more than a month's salary suddenly reads like a Swiggy order you spread across a year.
This is the whole trick, and it works on everyone. The sticker price disappears and your brain only sees the monthly number.
₹8,667 feels fine. You can do ₹8,667. What's ₹8,667 next to a salary.
You never once add it up. Because the day you add it up, you're holding a phone that cost you a month of work, and nobody wants to feel that when they're paying.
And it's not just phones. Indians spent ₹23.62 lakh crore on credit cards last year, up almost 12%. Monthly spends crossed ₹2 trillion in four separate months this year.
It means people got comfortable paying for today's thing with next month's money, one swipe at a time.
The funny part is nobody feels reckless doing it. No-cost EMI even sounds responsible. You're being smart. You're using the offer. You'd be a fool to pay upfront.
So the phone, the TV, the vacation, the kitchen appliance all become ₹8,667 a month. Twelve little numbers that each look harmless.
And then the 2nd of every month arrives and every one of them hits at once.
This is what the festive sale actually sells now. Not the discount. The permission to not think about the real price.
If you're building anything with a price tag in India, the real product isn't your product anymore. It's the monthly number you can make it shrink into.
The brand that wins this month isn't the one with the best phone. It's the one that made ₹99,900 feel like ₹8,667.

draft.caption: Be honest, do you check the full price anymore or just the EMI number?
draft.alt_text: A six-slide carousel arguing that the iPhone 17 topping India's sales charts is really a story about credit and EMI. It cites the phone's Big Billion Days price drop from ₹99,900 to about ₹77,999, no-cost EMI starting at ₹8,667 a month, and record credit card spending of ₹23.62 lakh crore in FY26, ending with what this means for brands pricing products in India.

claims.text: The iPhone 17 topped India's smartphone volume charts with over 4% market share
iPhone 17 price dropped to ₹77,999-79,999 against its ₹99,900 MRP during Big Billion Days
No-cost EMI options over 6 and 9 months with payments starting at ₹8,667 per month
India's credit card spending hit ₹23.62 lakh crore in FY2025-26, up nearly 12% from ₹21.09 lakh crore
Monthly credit card spends crossed ₹2 trillion in four separate months during FY2025-26

sources.fact: During Flipkart's Big Billion Days 2026, the iPhone 17 (256GB) price dropped to ₹79,999 (and ₹77,999 with bank card cashback) from its ₹99,900 listed price, backed by no-cost EMI offers.
sources.excerpt: The 256GB storage variant will receive a price cut and will drop down to Rs 79,999 during the sale period. Flipkart has listed the unit at Rs 99,900- this means that the platform is offering around Rs 20000 cut. That price further comes with Rs 2,500 off for credit card EMI payments (already included) and a Rs 3,000 flat exchange bonus. If you have a Flipkart Axis Bank or SBI credit card, then you can easily get additional cashback and discount, reducing the offered discounted price to Rs 77,999 with 5 per cent cashback. the e-commerce platform will offer no-cost options for 6 months and 9 months. So users can start with the payment at Rs 8,667 per month.

sources.fact: India's total credit card spending hit a record ₹23.62 trillion in FY2026, up 11.98% year-on-year, with monthly spends crossing ₹2 trillion multiple times during the year.
sources.excerpt: FY2026 total credit card spend: ₹23.62 trillion, up 11.98% year-on-year from ₹21.09 trillion in FY2025. This represents a deceleration from the prior year's expansion rate of 15.5%. The report indicates that monthly spending exceeded ₹2 trillion on multiple occasions during the fiscal year. Specifically, the data shows four separate months in 2025-26 when spending crossed this threshold—a significant achievement compared to earlier periods when such peaks were infrequent. March 2026: ₹2.19 trillion (described as "a three-month high"). December 2025: ₹2.05 trillion. January 2026: ₹2.00 trillion. The article notes that "each time monthly spending dips sharply...the following month tends to rebound strongly," illustrating the seasonal volatility characteristic of India's credit card market.

sources.fact: The iPhone 17 drove Apple's best-ever sales month in India, accounting for 57% of all iPhones sold — the highest-ever adoption rate for a new iPhone generation in the country, per Counterpoint.
sources.excerpt: Counterpoint's projections showed that the iPhone 17 accounted for 57% of all iPhones sold—the highest-ever adoption rate of Apple's latest generation smartphone in India to date.
